messages:
carmen: quick follow-up after yesterday's RFC review — proposing a compact operator playbook for shard warmup + signed-manifest handling. goal: predictable memory usage during mass rollouts and easy ops recovery.

noah: good. our last incident was basically a storage IO spike + simultaneous prefetches. any concrete mechanisms to prevent that?

carmen: yes. high-level plan: 1) require manifests to be signed (publisher signs manifest with key id). 2) loaders validate signature before prefetch. 3) prefetch uses prioritized, rate-limited wavefronts per-host. 4) warm pool capacity is reserved in advance (soft reserve) so swaps don't exceed GPU memory budget. 5) per-shard compatibility metadata is optional in manifest (initially off).

jin: on (4): how do we reserve without starving active models? soft reserve means we allocate but may evict lower-priority cold shards, right?

carmen: right. heuristic: warm_pool_reserve = min(0.15 * host_gpu_mem, model_shard_total_size). Eviction order: unused pinned shards -> lowest recent qps -> warm pool overflow. We avoid OOM by refusing a group swap if (current_used + warm_pool_reserve) > host_gpu_mem - oom_safety_margin.

noah: can we express this with config knobs? ops likes explicit numbers.

carmen: example config (stringified for ops):
```
"warmup": {
  "enable_signed_manifest": true,
  "warm_pool_fraction": 0.15,
  "oom_safety_margin_mb": 1024,
  "max_parallel_group_swaps": 1,
  "group_swap_size": 4,
  "prefetch_rate_limit_mb_s": 200
}
```

jin: signed manifests also help rollback attribution. Also think about manifest pinning TTL for in-flight traffic. customers sometimes pin models for long-running jobs. we should enforce a GC window.

carmen: propose pinned_ttl_ms default 300000 (5m). we keep pinned shards resident until pinned_ttl_ms since last pinned request. ops can extend via API.

ops-bot: note: metric "warmup.prefetch.backpressure" fired on infra-07 at 2025-08-12T09:14:22Z (avg prefetch latency 78ms > threshold 50ms).

noah: fallback strategies? in a full failure we need a safe fallback that doesn't change semantics. options: route to previous stable manifest; route to smaller quantized variant; or fail closed.

jin: prefer previous stable manifest for semantic stability, quantized fallback as secondary option. we should allow operators to configure per-model fallback policies.

carmen: ops API examples:
```
modelctl rollout --model-id=optic-v2 --manifest=sha256:ef12 --canary=0.05
modelctl rollout abort --op=rollout-8423
modelctl fallback set --model-id=optic-v2 --policy=previous-stable
```

noah: what about loader internals: atomic swap must be reader-safe. do we use RCU-like pointer swap with grace period?

carmen: yes: loader exposes an atomic pointer table per-shard. readers snapshot pointer; swap installs new pointer and increments generation. a background reclaimer waits for generation quiescence (requests finished) before freeing old memory. we also provide an aggressive reclaimer for low-memory situations (force-free after Xs with metrics & audit).

jin: and in-flight KV cache: we either invalidate per-shard on swap or maintain a compatibility shim. initial implementation: invalidate per-shard and warm the KV as requests arrive. easier and safer.

carmen: agreed. we'll document the tradeoff. win: simpler correctness; cost: short tail latency for first requests post-swap. ops can mitigate with longer canary and larger warm pool.

noah: telemetry we should emit: "shard.warmup.prefetch_latency_ms", "shard.warmup.bytes_fetched", "shard.swap.attempt", "shard.swap.success", "shard.swap.rollback", "warm_pool.usage_mb". add traces for per-shard hotpath.

ops-bot: warmup status: infra-09 prefetch: 16/64 shards warm; group 2 paused due to prefetch_rate_limit reached; suggested backoff 800ms.

carmen: last question — should manifest include an optional "compatibility_hint" map (layer_name -> compatible:true/false)? pros: allows smarter warmup & avoids invalidating caches when definitively compatible. cons: increases manifest complexity and requires publisher correctness. my vote: v1 - optional hint field but loader treats it as advisory only. we can introduce strict verification later.

jin: makes sense. ops can ignore hints unless they opt-in. add a flag to enforce_compat_hints=false by default.

noah: OK. summary: signed manifests + rate-limited prioritized prefetch + reserved warm pool + atomic pointer swap with generation reclamation + per-shard invalidation default + opsctl commands + metrics. ship a short follow-up doc and a small playbook for oncall.

carmen: I'll draft the follow-up and include a short playbook (how to abort, how to revert, which metrics to watch). pinging @jin @noah for review. thanks! :white_check_mark:
